name: Birkhoff's theorem for Einstein-Maxwell (in Misner-Sharp variables)

source.located: Classic: Jebsen 1921 (Ark. Mat. Ast. Fys. 15 nr.18), Birkhoff 1923 (Relativity and Modern Physics p.253) -- vacuum; the Einstein-Maxwell extension is attributed by Bronnikov-Melnikov (gr-qc/9403063, refs [2,3]) to Das 1960 (Progr. Theor. Phys. 24, 915) and Isaev 1976, and by Kubiznak-Svitek-Tahamtan (2605.01811) to Frolov-Zelnikov 2011 p.166 (Theorem 1, 'Generalized Birkhoff'). None of the read sources cites Hoffmann 1932, so that attribution is NOT confirmed here. Read exactly, on arXiv: (i) Hayward gr-qc/9408002, eqs (4), (11), (27), (28a-b) and Proposition 4 -- the Misner-Sharp energy, its variation formulas in general spherical symmetry with arbitrary T, and the vacuum Birkhoff proof from dE = 0; (ii) Bronnikov-Melnikov gr-qc/9403063 Theorem 1 with conditions A/B/C, special case (c) Abelian gauge field F_uK only (Einstein-Maxwell), and comments 4.3-4.4 giving the exceptions R = const and null gradient; (iii) Deser-Franklin gr-qc/0408067 (Weyl-method proof, m-dot = 0 as the gauge-varied field equation, history in note 5); (iv) Johansen-Ravndal physics/0508163 (history: Jebsen 1921 before Birkhoff 1923); (v) Weiner 2103.12178 Theorem 1 (T = -mu g_R + lambda g_S with mu = mu(r) => static with h = (r+c)/r - (2/r) INT 4 pi x^2 mu, i.e. exactly the electrovac shape rho = -p_r); (vi) Kubiznak-Svitek-Tahamtan 2605.01811 Theorem 1 (generalized Birkhoff: T_AB = (1/2) T^C_C gamma_AB with R non-constant => extra Killing vector) and its statement that Bertotti-Robinson is the non-asymptotically-flat exception.

published_statement: Vacuum (Hayward gr-qc/9408002 Prop. 4, verbatim): 'In vacuo, E is constant and the solution is locally isometric to the Schwarzschild solution with energy E. Proof. In vacuo, d_{+-}E = 0, so E is constant...' with E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)) and the general variation formula (11) d_{+-}E = 4 pi e^f r^2 (T_{+-} d_{+-} r - T_{+-+-} d_{-+} r), or in (tau, sigma) form (28a-b): E' = 4 pi r^2 (T_00 r' - T_01 rdot), Edot = 4 pi r^2 e^{-lambda}(T_01 r' - T_11 rdot). Einstein-Maxwell (Bronnikov-Melnikov gr-qc/9403063 Theorem 1 + special case (c)): for metric ds^2 = eta_u e^{2 alpha} du^2 + eta_v e^{2 gamma} dv^2 + e^{2 beta} dOmega^2 obeying Einstein's equations, if (A) the gradient of rho = 2 beta (log area) is non-null and non-zero in a domain, (B) [trivial for one internal space], (C) in the frame with rho = rho(u), T_uv = 0 and a combination T^v_v + const T^u_u is independent of v and gamma, then there is an orthogonal frame in which the metric is v-independent; an Abelian gauge field with the single component F_uK (K != v), for which T^u_u = T^K_K = -F^{uK}F_{uK}, satisfies (C) -- 'Coulomb-like fields for spherical ... symmetries' are named. Kubiznak-Svitek-Tahamtan 2605.01811 Theorem 1 (from Frolov-Zelnikov p.166): 'If the energy-momentum tensor generating a spherically symmetric gravitational field of the form ds^2 = gamma_AB dx^A dx^B + R(x)^2 dOmega^2, where ... R(x) is a non-constant function, obeys T_AB = (1/2) T^C_C gamma_AB, then the corresponding solution of the Einstein equations possesses an additional Killing vector field', and in the asymptotically flat Maxwell case the unique solution is Reissner-Nordstrom f = 1 - 2M/r + Q^2/r^2 (their eq. (18) at L = -S/2). The conclusion the tree actually uses -- the mass function m(R) = M - Q^2/(2R) with M a constant, for any spherically symmetric electrovac spacetime -- is the dE-integration step of these proofs (Hayward (11)/(28) with the Maxwell T), NOT the staticity/Killing-vector conclusion.
published_hypotheses: H1 Spherical symmetry: metric of warped-product form gamma_AB(x) dx^A dx^B + R(x)^2 dOmega^2 (Hayward eq. (1) double-null; Bronnikov-Melnikov eq. (3); Kubiznak et al. eq. (14)).
H2 Einstein's equations G_ab = 8 pi T_ab hold (Hayward Sec. III first sentence; Bronnikov-Melnikov eq. (1)).

H3 Source: pure Maxwell field, source-free (no charged matter, no current) -- Bronnikov-Melnikov (c): 'Abelian gauge fields ... under the restriction that the vector potential U_A has a single nonzero component U_K(u)'; Kubiznak et al. eq. (16) A = phi dt + p cos(theta) dphi with dF = 0 and d*D = 0. Only F_tr and F_thph survive spherical symmetry; both give T^t_t = T^r_r and T_tr = 0.

H4 For the FULL theorem (staticity / local RN): the areal radius R is non-constant with non-null gradient in the domain (Bronnikov-Melnikov condition A; Kubiznak et al. 'R(x) is a non-constant function ... crucial'; 4.3-4.4 show R = const and null-gradient cases are genuine exceptions -- Bertotti-Robinson AdS2 x S2 is the electrovac one).

H5 For the FROZEN-MASS statement alone (the part the tree uses): H1-H3 only. Hayward's variation formula (11)/(28) needs no assumption on dr; it is an identity of the Einstein tensor, and with the Maxwell T it integrates to E = M - Q^2/2r with M constant on any connected domain.

H6 Local statement: 'All arguments will be local' (Hayward Sec. I); asymptotic flatness is NOT a hypothesis (it is a conclusion of Weiner's Theorem 3 only under further conditions), and BR shows the non-asymptotically-flat electrovac branch exists.
hypothesis_drift: NAME > CONTENT (drivensource.py:100-102, 519-523): the tree calls its result 'Birkhoff's theorem for Einstein-Maxwell', but what it checks and uses is only the frozen-mass part (M constant), not the staticity / extra-Killing-vector / local-RN conclusion. This is a narrowing of the CONCLUSION, not a weakening of hypotheses: the part used holds on a LARGER class than the full theorem (it needs no dR != 0 -- see Bertotti-Robinson witness, rederivation section 7, where dR = 0, the spacetime is not RN, and m = Q/2 = M - Q^2/2Q still). Not a fault; recorded so the label is not later read as a claim of staticity.

ADDED HYPOTHESIS (drivensource.py:81, 297-306): the diagonal ansatz ds^2 = -e^{2Phi}dt^2 + e^{2Lambda}dr^2 + R^2 dOmega^2 with no dt dr cross term. Locally any spherically symmetric 2-metric gamma_AB can be diagonalised (Deser-Franklin eq. (10) start from the 4-function form and diagonalise), so this loses no generality for a local statement. Deser-Franklin Sec. II-IV also show that dropping the off-diagonal function BEFORE varying an action loses the Birkhoff equation -- but the tree works from the field equations (the MS equations), not an action, so this caution does not bite. The MS equations are rebuilt here from the Einstein tensor (rederivation section 1) with the same ansatz, and they are identities.

PHRASING 'for ARBITRARY Phi(t,r), Lambda(t,r) and R(t,r)' (drivensource.py:100-101, 522): what is computed is that the two MS residuals vanish when m = M - Q^2/2R is SUBSTITUTED as an independent function. In an actual solution m is not independent: 1 - 2m/R = e^{-2Lambda}R'^2 - e^{-2Phi}Rdot^2 constrains (Phi, Lambda, R), and the remaining Einstein equations reduce the metric to RN (or BR). The correct reading, and the one the tree's conclusion needs, is: the MS equations viewed as a first-order system for m(t,r) have the unique solution M - Q^2/2R whatever the metric functions are. Discrepancy of wording only; the conclusion 'no motion of the metric functions changes m at a given areal radius' is exactly right.

UNIQUENESS ASSERTED, NOT CHECKED (drivensource.py:96 'the solution is exact'): the owner substitutes and checks; it does not show that M - Q^2/2R is the ONLY solution. Rederivation section 5 closes this: e^{Lambda}(MS-r residual) = d_r(m + Q^2/2R) and e^{Phi}(MS-t residual) = d_t(m + Q^2/2R) identically, so the residuals vanish iff m + Q^2/2R is constant. One line, now machine-checked. No drift in the conclusion.

Q CONSTANT ASSUMED (drivensource.py:296 'Q = sp.Symbol'): the owner takes Q a constant and verifies the Maxwell residuals vanish; that Q MUST be constant is not shown. Rederivation section 2 leaves Q = Q(t,r) free and finds the two non-trivial source-free Maxwell residuals are +sin(theta) d_r Q and -sin(theta) d_t Q, so Q constant is DERIVED from Maxwell's equations (this is the 'vector Birkhoff theorem -- constancy of electric charge' of Deser-Franklin Sec. II). No drift in the conclusion.

DROPPED CASE, COMMENT ONLY (drivensource.py:302 'Spherical symmetry admits only F_{tr} (radial electric)'): spherical symmetry also admits the radial magnetic component F_thph = P sin(theta) (Kubiznak et al. eq. (16) 'p cos(theta) dphi'; Bronnikov-Melnikov 'and their magnetic counterparts'). Rederivation section 6: with (Q, P) the Maxwell residuals still vanish, rho = (Q^2 + P^2)/(8 pi R^4), j = 0, p_r = -rho, and m = M - (Q^2 + P^2)/2R satisfies both MS equations. The conclusion survives with Q^2 -> Q^2 + P^2; the comment at line 302 is a discrepancy, not a refutation. SCOPE (line 459) says 'pure electrovac' which covers the dyonic case, so the status words are not wrong, only the comment.

OWNER'S INFERENCE OUTSIDE THE THEOREM (drivensource.py:104-107, 454-456, 616-620; specthm.py:877-878, 894-898): 'the driven branch has no electromagnetic degree of freedom to drive it' and EM_CAN_SOURCE_DRIVEN_CONTRACTION = False. The theorem gives m frozen. It does NOT by itself forbid nonstatic.py's contraction inequality 2m/R < e^{-2Phi} Rdot^2 from holding: rederivation section 8 exhibits RN in a moving geodesic slicing (Phi = 0, R = R(r - t), infall energy E) that satisfies G = 8 pi T exactly, has m = M - Q^2/2R frozen, and has contraction variable W = E > 1 with rho > 0 -- exactly what Milne does for vacuum in nonstatic.py. What closes the driven branch is the tree's own two-step inference (a driven contraction that is a DESTINATION needs m(R) to evolve; a moving areal radius is not a destination, nonstatic.py section 0 and 6). That inference is consistent with the tree's own vacuum reasoning and is not contradicted here; it is simply not part of the external result and is not graded by this audit. Recorded so that 'Birkhoff closes the driven branch' is read as 'Birkhoff + nonstatic.py's destination argument close it'.

KEPT CORRECTLY: 'A charged fluid is a different tensor and is NOT covered' (drivensource.py:109-110) matches H3 (T_tr = 0 and T^t_t = T^r_r fail for charged matter with current or pressure); SCOPE at 459-460 excludes non-spherical fields and nonlinear electrodynamics -- Bronnikov-Melnikov (d) and Kubiznak et al. Theorem 1 in fact EXTEND the frozen-mass/staticity result to any L(S,P) nonlinear electrodynamics with the same ansatz, so the tree's scope is narrower than the theorem's reach, which is the safe direction.

rederivation.outcome: 28/28 checks pass, exit 0, ~10 s, sympy 1.14.0 (log: .../d67/rederive/run.log). Independent of the tree (nothing imported from research/). (1) MS-r and MS-t rebuilt from the Einstein tensor of the diagonal ansatz are identities (residual 0). (2) With Q = Q(t,r) free, the source-free Maxwell residuals are +sin(theta) d_r Q and -sin(theta) d_t Q: Q constant is derived. (3) Maxwell T in the full dynamical metric: rho = Q^2/8 pi R^4, j = 0, p_r = -rho, p_T = +rho (agrees with drivensource.py:85). (4) The owner's substitution check reproduced: both residuals 0 with m = M - Q^2/2R. (5) Uniqueness: e^{Lambda}(MS-r) = d_r(m + Q^2/2R), e^{Phi}(MS-t) = d_t(m + Q^2/2R) identically, so m + Q^2/2R is constant -- the step the owner asserts at line 96 is now checked. (6) Dyonic case: conclusion holds with Q^2 -> Q^2 + P^2; the owner's line-302 comment 'only F_tr' is a discrepancy. (7) Bertotti-Robinson (Phi = ln(Q cosh r), Lambda = ln Q, R = Q): exact electrovac solution, dR = 0, m = Q/2 = M - Q^2/2Q -- the exception to full Birkhoff where the frozen-mass form still holds. (8) RN in a moving geodesic slicing (Phi = 0, e^{2 Lambda} = (E^2 - f(R))/E^2, R' = -Rdot = sqrt(E^2 - f(R))): G = 8 pi T exactly, m = M - Q^2/2R frozen, W = E, U = -sqrt(E^2 - f) != 0.

later_literature.ref: Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', gr-qc/9408002 (Phys. Rev. D 53, 1938, 1996)
later_literature.what: Gives the Misner-Sharp energy variation formulas (11), (28a-b) for ARBITRARY spherically symmetric T with no staticity assumption, and proves vacuum Birkhoff from dE = 0 (Prop. 4). The tree's MS-r/MS-t are the (tau, sigma)-form (28a-b) in the (Phi, Lambda, R) notation; the electrovac integration is the same step with T_00 = -T_11 e^{...} = rho.

later_literature.ref: Bronnikov & Melnikov, 'The Birkhoff theorem in multidimensional gravity', gr-qc/9403063 (1994); restates Bronnikov & Kovalchuk J. Phys. A 13, 187 (1980)
later_literature.what: Theorem 1: sufficient conditions (A) non-null non-zero gradient of the areal function, (C) T_uv = 0 and a v-independent combination of T^u_u, T^v_v, for the metric to be v-independent; special case (c) Abelian gauge field with one component (Einstein-Maxwell) and (d) any nonlinear L(F^2) (Born-Infeld) satisfy (C). Comments 4.3-4.4 exhibit the exceptions R = const (spheres of equal radii, nonlinear wave equation) and null gradient, and state 'no condition may be omitted or essentially weakened'.

later_literature.ref: Deser & Franklin, 'Schwarzschild and Birkhoff a la Weyl', gr-qc/0408067 (Am. J. Phys. 73, 261, 2005)
later_literature.what: Proves m-dot = 0 as the field equation obtained by varying the off-diagonal metric function (eq. (26)), with the Maxwell analogue q-dot = 0 from varying A_r (eq. (4)) -- the two constancy statements the tree's frozen-mass result combines. Caution (Sec. II, IV): dropping the off-diagonal function BEFORE varying an action loses this equation; the tree works from field equations, so it is unaffected. History note 5: Jebsen 1921, Alexandrow 1923, Eiesland 1925.

later_literature.ref: Johansen & Ravndal, 'On the discovery of Birkhoff's theorem', physics/0508163 (Gen. Rel. Grav. 38, 537, 2006)
later_literature.what: History only: Jebsen derived the theorem 'directly from Einstein's field equation' in 1921, Birkhoff in 1923. No statement about the Einstein-Maxwell extension, so Hoffmann 1932 remains unconfirmed by any read source.

Theorem 1: a spherically symmetric spacetime with T = -mu g_R + lambda g_S (i.e. rho = -p_r = mu, exactly the electrovac shape) has mu = mu(r), is static, and h = 1 - 2m(r)/r with m(r) = c + INT 4 pi x^2 mu dx (Remark p.17) -- for mu = Q^2/8 pi r^4 this is m = M - Q^2/2r. Hypotheses (Sec. 2): r regular (dr != 0) and used as a coordinate, so the BR exception is excluded by assumption, as in the classic. Also gives the anisotropic-TOV form (28) and Corollary 3 that spherically symmetric dust cannot be static.

later_literature.ref: Kubiznak, Svitek & Tahamtan, 'Bertotti-Robinson and Bonnor-Melvin universes in nonlinear electrodynamics', arXiv:2605.01811 (2026)
later_literature.what: Restates the generalized Birkhoff theorem (Frolov-Zelnikov 2011 p.166) with the explicit hypothesis 'R(x) is a non-constant function ... crucial', applies it to any L(S,P) nonlinear electrodynamics (electric + magnetic, eq. (16)), gives the unique asymptotically flat metric (18), and derives the R = const branch: generalized Bertotti-Robinson AdS2 x S2 with unequal radii unless the NLE is conformally invariant (Theorem 2); Maxwell BR has R_0^2 = e^2 + p^2. Confirms that the tree's SCOPE exclusion of NLE is conservative -- the frozen-mass/staticity result extends there.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis ('some previous physicists may have all lacked certain data') tested against this result: the theorem has no data input at all. Jebsen (1921) and Birkhoff (1923) had Einstein's equations and the Schwarzschild solution; the electrovac extension needed only the Reissner (1916) / Nordstrom (1918) solution and Maxwell's equations, all available before 1923. No measured constant, no experimental bound and no later observation enters any hypothesis or conclusion, so nothing that came later could have changed it; what came later (Bronnikov-Kovalchuk 1980, Hayward 1996, Weiner 2021, Kubiznak et al. 2026) sharpened the HYPOTHESES (non-null non-constant areal gradient) and located the exceptions (Bertotti-Robinson, null-gradient waves) rather than moving the conclusion. Evidence against the hypothesis for this item: the rederivation reproduces the conclusion from the field equations alone in ~10 s with no datum. The one genuine limitation the classics under-stated -- that the areal radius must be a good coordinate -- does not touch the part the tree uses, which holds even at the exception (section 7). Where data could matter is the OWNER'S next step, not this theorem: whether a real charged configuration can be a 'destination', which is an engineering question the tree already routes through nonstatic.py's destination argument, not through Birkhoff.
grade_evidence: The statement AS USED -- for any spherically symmetric source-free Einstein-Maxwell configuration, in any (Phi, Lambda, R) slicing, the Misner-Sharp mass is m = M - Q^2/(2R) with M constant, so m at a given areal radius cannot be driven -- is (a) the dE-integration step of Hayward's Prop. 4 with the Maxwell T, read at source; (b) a corollary of Bronnikov-Melnikov Theorem 1 case (c) and of Weiner Theorem 1, read at source; (c) re-derived here independently of the tree with 28/28 sympy checks including the two steps the owner did not check (Q constant is forced by Maxwell; the solution is unique because e^{Lambda}MS-r and e^{Phi}MS-t are the exact partials of m + Q^2/2R). Its hypotheses (spherical symmetry, EFE, source-free Maxwell) are exactly the owner's SCOPE, and it holds on a LARGER class than the full theorem (it survives the Bertotti-Robinson exception, where full Birkhoff fails). No datum enters. Three discrepancies are recorded and none is a refutation: the label 'Birkhoff's theorem' names more than is used (staticity is neither checked nor needed); the line-302 comment 'only F_tr' omits the magnetic component, under which the conclusion holds with Q^2 -> Q^2 + P^2; and the phrase 'for ARBITRARY Phi, Lambda, R' describes the residual computation, not an independence of m from the metric. The downstream step 'therefore the driven branch is closed' (EM_CAN_SOURCE_DRIVEN_CONTRACTION = False) is the owner's inference, not this external result: section 8 shows the contraction inequality W > 1 CAN hold in a moving slicing of RN with the mass frozen, exactly as in the tree's own Milne witness, so that closure rests on nonstatic.py's 'moving areal radius is not a destination' argument in addition to Birkhoff. That is consistent with the tree and is left for the owner's own audit item.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: a spherically symmetric source-free Einstein-Maxwell configuration in the diagonal ansatz whose Misner-Sharp mass is not of the form M - Q^2/2R with M constant -- rederivation section 5 shows this is impossible on any connected domain, so it would require breaking H1-H3 (charged matter, a current, non-spherical field, a different theory) which the owner already excludes. To WRONG: a computed counterexample within H1-H3; none exists since the uniqueness is an exact identity. To DATA-DEPENDENT: not possible, no datum enters. The grade would also have to be revisited if the owner's status words were read as claiming STATICITY of every spherically symmetric electrovac spacetime -- that stronger claim needs dR non-null and non-constant (Bronnikov-Melnikov A) and fails on Bertotti-Robinson; the owner does not currently make it, but the label 'Birkhoff's theorem' invites it.
